The oven itself was rectangular and had a width-length ratio of W/L.
There was also a weighting criteria p and 1 − p, where 0 ≤ p ≤ 1.

Tessellating patterns for squares and hexagons The lattice packing algorithm calculates twice the apothem for regular polygons with multiple of 4 sides, with the exception of squares, and then checked to see how many polygons could be fit into a particular length and width shaped oven.
L·W This allowed for there to be space between the squares when they were put into the oven to insure airflow between the baking pans.
Diagram showing the side length (S), apothem (r), and Radius (R) of a regular polygon.

Determining the surface area of each data point for heating One of the most difficult problems to solve for our heating model was determining how much surface area each small volume of brownie batter had with the pan.
initially considered just drawing the shape of the pan over a grid and determining how much area fell into each grid space.

The problem with this approach was that some edge squares only had a little bit of surface area associated with them simply because of how the grid fell, not because of any characteristics of the geometry of the pan.
